decontamination_notes: Real ETag-parsing hardening from pallets/werkzeug PR #3234 ('discard invalid etag values', https://github.com/pallets/werkzeug/pull/3234), merged 2026-08-10 -- after the training cutoffs of the models evaluated here (e.g. Opus 5, May 2026), so the specific fix is not in their training data (decontaminated: true), with upstream_merged recorded as proof. ETag headers (If-Match / If-None-Match) are parsed into an ETags collection used for conditional-request decisions. The parser accepted invalid *unquoted* values alongside well-formed quoted ETags (the header regex had an `([^" \t,]+)` invalid-unquoted-value branch), so a malformed entry became a real ETag that could satisfy a match it should not, and ETags membership did not guard against a None unquote result. The fix parses only syntactically valid quoted ETags (dropping the invalid branch across werkzeug/http.py and sansio/http.py) and makes ETags.__contains__ reject None values (etag.py). werkzeug is pure Python; its package __init__ imports MarkupSafe, so MarkupSafe is vendored into repo/_vendor (built for the sandbox's linux-amd64) and hidden tests run offline with PYTHONPATH=src:_vendor on the base image; parse_etags is deprecated (a warning, not an error) so tests pass -W ignore::DeprecationWarning. Repo sliced at the PR base commit (src/, 22.3k LOC; parser still keeping invalid unquoted values); BSD-3-Clause LICENSE preserved. Coverage floor: 3 fail_to_pass (an invalid unquoted value is discarded from the set; an invalid value does not match; an all-invalid header parses to empty) plus a 2-check regression guard (valid quoted ETags still parse; a valid ETag still matches by value).
